title.en: Design a 1-bit comparator from its truth table
Compare multi-bit numbers starting from the MSB

say.en: A digital thermostat compares the room temperature with the set value; a lift compares the floor it is on with the floor you pressed. The circuit behind it is a magnitude comparator. In this lesson: Design a 1-bit comparator from its truth table.
Compare multi-bit numbers starting from the MSB.
Know the 4-bit comparator IC 7485.

body.en: A *magnitude comparator* compares two binary numbers A and B and gives three outputs: A > B, A = B and A < B; exactly one is 1. For single bits: $(A>B) = A\bar{B}$, $(A<B) = \bar{A}B$ and $(A=B) = \overline{A\oplus B} = AB + \bar{A}\bar{B}$ (an XNOR gate). It is a combinational circuit: two AND gates with inverters and one XNOR gate.

points.en: A = B: XNOR of A and B

narration.en: A one-bit comparator gives A greater than B as A B-bar, A less than B as A-bar B, and A equal to B as the XNOR of A and B.

body.en: For 4-bit numbers, define $x_i = \overline{A_i\oplus B_i}$ (1 when bit i is equal). Then $(A=B) = x_3x_2x_1x_0$. The numbers are compared from the MSB: $(A>B) = A_3\bar{B_3} + x_3A_2\bar{B_2} + x_3x_2A_1\bar{B_1} + x_3x_2x_1A_0\bar{B_0}$, and $(A<B)$ similarly with $\bar{A_i}B_i$. The first unequal bit from the left decides. IC 7485 is a 4-bit magnitude *comparator* with cascading inputs for longer numbers.
